questions.question: If a vehicle is about to hit you from behind, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head firmly against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, your body will move backward. Press yourself against your seat and push your head against the head restraint to prevent injury. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn.
Turn right at the intersection.
Parking area ahead.
Crossroad ahead. Watch for traffic.

questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a crossroad is coming.

questions.question: When the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line next to your lane, when can you pass?

options.text: Only in an emergency.
If you are on an expressway.
If traffic is clear.
Only at an intersection.

questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is next to your lane, you can pass if no vehicles are coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: What does a single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Lanes move in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Lanes move in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Lanes move in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Lanes move in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes move in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what should you do?

options.text: Enter faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up. Signal, look for an opening, speed up to match traffic, then merge safely.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means passing is allowed from that lane only.

questions.question: How should you always view railroad crossings?

options.text: Safe to cross because trains rarely come.
Dangerous.
Safe places to park.
Places where you must always stop.

questions.explanation: Always treat railroad crossings as dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and instructions from flaggers. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Any lights work the same.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within your headlight beam.
Use high beam headlights to see cars ahead better.
Keep dashboard lights bright so other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within your headlight beam.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day. You cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect how far your vehicle takes to stop?

options.text: Steering ability.
Braking distance.
Reaction distance.
Perception time.

questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on speed and road conditions.

questions.question: When should you move back into the right lane after passing another vehicle?

options.text: When you are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.
When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You need enough space to return safely to the right lane. When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, there is enough distance between you and that vehicle to change lanes safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Yield the right-of-way.
Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign is posted on one-way streets and other roads where you cannot enter. You may see this sign if you try to enter an expressway ramp going the wrong direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for people crossing your path.
No passing zone.
Work zone ahead.

questions.explanation: This orange warning sign tells you that road work is coming. Stay alert for temporary traffic signs and equipment in the work zone.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, what should you do?

options.text: Always insist on the right-of-way over vehicles when using a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
Enter a crosswalk at any time because it is the driver's responsibility to stop.
Use crosswalks only if they are convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming toward you. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a vehicle that is too close may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: What is important to do before turning left?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Yield to oncoming vehicles.
Swing to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first. You do not have the right-of-way in this situation.

questions.question: When you cannot see clearly while driving, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.explanation: The first thing you should do when visibility is poor is slow down. This helps you stay safe in bad driving conditions.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Come to a stop.
Go straight ahead.

questions.explanation: When a driver holds their left arm straight up, they are signaling that they will turn right. Adjust your driving if you are behind this driver.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?

options.text: You are not required to stop.
You must slow down to check if traffic is clear.
You should stop at a spot where you can see 200 feet in each direction, even if you enter the other road.
You should stop where you can clearly see oncoming traffic before you enter the other road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should stop where you can clearly see oncoming traffic before you enter the other road.
questions.explanation: Stop at the spot closest to the other road where you can see traffic coming. Do not enter the other road to get a better view.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do?

options.text: Start to prepare to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Sound a sharp blast of your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
questions.explanation: Use a sharp horn blast when a child or pedestrian is about to step into the street in front of your car. This alerts them to the danger.

questions.question: Is it safe to use cruise control on snowy or icy roads if you reduce your speed?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snowy or icy roads. Your tires may slip and lose grip on the road, and you will lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Your body removes approximately how much alcohol per hour?

options.text: Three alcoholic drinks per hour.
One alcoholic drink per hour.
Two alcoholic drinks per hour.
None of the above.

questions.explanation: The average person's body processes about one drink per hour. However, how impaired you become depends on many factors. These include how much you drink, how fast you drink it, your body weight, whether you have eaten, and your overall health.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing in any marked or unmarked crosswalk. For safety, always yield to anyone crossing any street.

questions.question: When entering the highway on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, you should:

options.text: Enter the far-right lane immediately and speed up to match traffic flow.
Use the shoulder to speed up to match traffic.
Speed up and enter only after you find a gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up and enter only after you find a gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering the highway on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, only speed up after you see a gap in traffic. You should wait and be stopped while looking for a safe gap.

questions.question: A single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Lanes move in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Lanes move in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A dashed line means drivers next to it can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location. Making a right turn here would be unsafe and against the law.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, you should:

options.text: Keep wheels straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels sharply to the left, away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your car will roll into the curb, not into traffic.

questions.question: If you have a sudden tire blowout, you should:

options.text: Use the brakes lightly.
Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes firmly.

questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the car going straight. Slow down gradually by easing off the gas and using light brake pressure.

questions.question: Regulatory signs:

options.text: Are placed wherever there is immediate danger.
Tell drivers what they must or must not do.
Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
May warn drivers about school zones ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell drivers what they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black text on white backgrounds. They tell drivers what they must or must not do. Examples include speed limits, no passing, and no turning signs.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. You should:

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see where it is.
Slow down but don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see where it is.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren nearby but don't know where the emergency vehicle is, pull safely to the right side and stop. Wait until you are sure the vehicle is not coming toward you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge right.
Divided highway begins.
Lane ends.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you the right lane is ending ahead. Drivers in that lane will need to merge into another lane.
